To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we report a male sibling pair with a novel PORCN mutation in non-mosaic state and a phenotype overlapping FDH.
we report a novel, inherited PORCN mutation in two male siblings with overlapping FDH and other anomalies.

we identified a novel mutation in the PORC N gene in two male siblings with overlapping skeletal, ocular, renal and skin malformations and that this is the second report of a nonmosaic male with a PORCN mutation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterization of novel mutations in the PORC N gene in patients with FDH and other PORCN-related disorders.
the clinical and molecular genetic characterization of a male with multiple congenital malformations, overlapping with the X-linked dominant FDH.
the identification of a novel mutation in the PORC gene in a non-mosaically male patient, which has not been reported before.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this is the second case of a non-mosiacic male with a PORCN mutation and the first one with an inherited mutation.
this case represents the second case of an inherited non-mosaic PORC N mutation in a male patient.
the mutation in the present case is not a de novo mutation and is not a mosaic.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PORCN mutations can be associated with a spectrum of phenotypes, ranging from focal dermal hypoplaisia to the more severe condition of the reported cases.
the p.Ser250PHE mutation is likely to be pathogenic and the phenotype in this patient is consistent with an X-linked recessively inherited condition.
the PORCN gene is a candidate for the diagnosis of patients with multiple congenital abnormalities overlapping with FDH.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PORCN gene is not a lethal gene in the absence of mosaicism.
